officialDocs.label: Packaging and distributing External Client Apps (Trailhead)

verdict.summary: No review is required to let other orgs connect, but since Spring '26 new integrations are built as External Client Apps, which are local to your org unless you ship them in a 2GP managed package, and since September 2025 users can't authorize an app that isn't installed in their org without a special permission. In practice every customer's admin installs your package (or grants 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps'), and the customer needs an edition with API access (Enterprise and up, or a paid add-on on Professional).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: A free Developer Edition org plus a Local External Client App with the api and refresh_token scopes. No review or verification for your own org.

timeToProd.assumes: A Packaged External Client App in a self-built 2GP managed package that each customer admin installs via URL, with no AppExchange listing; an AppExchange listing adds a paid security review of several weeks.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing from Salesforce for unlisted distribution. Each customer's admin installing the package (or granting the bypass permission) before their users can connect.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The range covers setting up Dev Hub + namespace orgs, packaging, and promoting a version. Customer admin turnaround is outside your control and not included.

verdict.cost: Free to build and distribute unlisted. Customers need API access (included in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, Developer; paid add-on for Professional). AppExchange security review is a paid, optional step for listing.

prerequisites.item: Two free Developer Edition orgs: one with Dev Hub enabled, one with a registered namespace
prerequisites.why: A Packaged External Client App lives in a 2GP managed package, which needs a Dev Hub and a linked namespace. Enabling Dev Hub can't be undone.
Used to retrieve the External Client App metadata, create the package and promote package versions.

prerequisites.item: Customers on an edition with API access, with users who have the API Enabled permission
prerequisites.why: Group, Essentials and Professional editions don't include API access by default; Professional can buy it as an add-on. Calls from an org without it fail with API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From search snippets of Salesforce's REST API 'Supported Editions' page; the page returned HTTP 403 to our fetcher so we could not read it directly.

prerequisites.why: Configured on the External Client App's OAuth settings and matched on the authorize and token calls.

scopeTiers.impact: Sign-in and user identity. Still subject to the installed-app restriction in the customer's org.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Scopes observed in scopes_supported of login.salesforce.com's OIDC discovery document.

scopeTiers.tier: Core data access (what most agents need)
scopeTiers.impact: Read and write records through REST/SOAP/Bulk as the connecting user, limited by that user's profile and sharing rules. No Salesforce review, but the customer needs API access in their edition.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Nango lists api + refresh_token/offline_access as the minimum scopes.

scopeTiers.impact: Only useful if the customer owns the matching product (Data Cloud, Account Engagement, etc.). An mcp_api scope is advertised.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Scope names are tested from the discovery document; the licensing dependency is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: Grants everything the user can access. Customer admins and AppExchange security reviewers are likely to push back; prefer api.

steps.title: Sign up for Developer Edition orgs
steps.detail: Create two free Developer Edition orgs. Enable Dev Hub in the first (irreversible) and register a namespace in the second, then link the namespace from the Dev Hub's Namespace Registries.

steps.title: Create the External Client App
steps.detail: In the Dev Hub: Setup > App Manager > New External Client App. Set Distribution State to Packaged (Local works only inside this org), enable OAuth, set the callback URL, add api and refresh_token/offline_access, enable Authorization Code and Credentials Flow, keep PKCE and secret requirements on.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: New Connected Apps can't be created by default since Spring '26.

steps.title: Copy credentials and set the refresh token policy
steps.detail: Settings tab > OAuth Settings > Consumer Key and Secret (identity verification may be asked). On the Policies tab, set Refresh Token Policy to 'valid until revoked' if you need long-lived access.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth web server flow
steps.detail: Authorize at https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize (test.salesforce.com for sandboxes, or the customer's My Domain), exchange the code at /services/oauth2/token with PKCE, and store instance_url per connection: every API call goes to that customer-specific host.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Endpoints observed in the discovery document; instance_url handling is from Nango's guide.

steps.title: Generate package metadata
steps.detail: Write package.xml with ExternalClientApplication, ExtlClntAppOauthSettings and ExtlClntAppOauthConfigurablePolicies, retrieve with sf project retrieve start, and configure sfdx-project.json with the namespace and package alias.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: OAuth consumer credentials are global settings and are not packaged.

steps.title: Create and promote a managed package version
steps.detail: Run sf package create --package-type Managed, then sf package version create, then promote the version so it can be installed in production orgs. Keep the install URL.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Nango shows create/version steps; the need to promote before production installs is our understanding of 2GP and wasn't stated in the sources we opened.

steps.title: Write customer admin install instructions
steps.detail: Explain: install the package via URL (admins only), set the app's policies (permitted users, profiles/permission sets), and confirm API access in their edition. Offer the fallback of temporarily granting 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps'.

steps.title: Customer admin installs the package
steps.detail: Each customer org's admin installs your package before end users can authorize. This is on the customer's timeline.

steps.title: Optional: AppExchange listing and security review
steps.detail: Join the partner program, submit for security review and list on AppExchange for discoverability and customer trust. Not needed to let customers connect.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Search snippets of the ISVforce guide mention a report about 3–4 weeks after submission and a fee for paid apps; the pages returned HTTP 403 so we could not confirm the current figures.

agentCanDo: Implement the web server flow with PKCE, instance_url storage and token refresh
Generate package.xml and sfdx-project.json for the External Client App
Run sf CLI packaging commands once a human has authenticated the Dev Hub
Write customer admin install and permission instructions
Handle API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG and daily-limit errors gracefully

Create the External Client App and copy the consumer key and secret

blockers.cause: Since September 2025, users can't authorize a connected app that isn't installed in their org unless they hold 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' (or 'Use Any API Client').
blockers.fix: Have the customer admin install your package, or temporarily grant the permission to the authorizing user, authorize, then remove it.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Error string reported by a vendor (MoveData) support page.

blockers.symptom: No 'New Connected App' option in App Manager, or creation is refused
blockers.cause: Spring '26 disabled creation of new Connected Apps by default in all orgs, in both UI and API.
blockers.fix: Create an External Client App instead. Support can grant a temporary exception, which Salesforce says will go away.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Third-party vendor docs; we didn't open Salesforce's own release note.

blockers.symptom: Users in other orgs can't use your External Client App at all
blockers.cause: Distribution State is Local, which works only in the org where the app was created. Sandboxes support only Local.
blockers.fix: Create the app with Distribution State Packaged in a non-sandbox org and distribute it in a 2GP managed package.

blockers.symptom: API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG on API calls after a successful login
blockers.cause: The customer's edition (Group, Essentials, Professional without add-on) doesn't include API access, or the user lacks API Enabled.
blockers.fix: Tell the customer to upgrade or buy the API add-on, and to assign API Enabled to integration users.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From search snippets of Salesforce's supported-editions page, which returned 403 to our fetcher.

blockers.symptom: Integration stops working after a few hours or days
blockers.cause: The app's refresh token policy expires tokens, or the admin revoked the token or changed app policies.
blockers.fix: Set Refresh Token Policy to 'valid until revoked' and handle invalid_grant by prompting reconnection.

blockers.symptom: Device-flow authorization blocked even for users who previously authorized
blockers.cause: Uninstalled apps using the OAuth 2.0 device flow are blocked for all users under the September 2025 change.
blockers.fix: Use the web server flow and have the app installed in the customer org.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Seen in search-result summaries of vendor posts; not confirmed in a page we opened.

nuances.text: Every customer has its own instance_url (My Domain host). Store it per connection and send API calls there, not to login.salesforce.com. Sandboxes authorize via test.salesforce.com.

OAuth consumer credentials are 'global settings' kept in your long-lived org and not packaged. A subscriber org can reuse them or generate its own, which breaks the link to your app's global settings.
Connected Apps are 'globally available by default'; External Client Apps are 'local by default'. Existing Connected Apps keep working, and Salesforce lists no deprecation date for them.
The agent acts with the connecting user's permissions and sharing. A dedicated integration user per customer org is common, which affects which data the agent can see.
Customer orgs have a daily API request allocation shared by all integrations, so a chatty agent can exhaust it.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: General Salesforce knowledge; the API limits page wasn't opened (developer.salesforce.com returned 403).

nuances.text: Admins can enable API Access Control (requested through the account executive), which blocks uninstalled apps outright and restricts which users can use each app.
Salesforce exposes dynamic client registration and introspection endpoints, plus mcp_api and a2a_api scopes, in its OIDC discovery document.
